 Judgment
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 28.12.2015 at about 15.30 hours when the deceased Kisan S/o: Tukaram Shivasharan and his friend Mahesh Dhavare after attending a function at Salagar(B), Tq: Mangalaweda, were returning on their motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-13/9787 to Mangalaweda.

The deceased Kisan was riding the motorcycle in a moderate speed and on the extreme left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and his friend Mahesh was pillion rider of the said motorcycle.

When the said motorcycle came near the land of Siddappa Talegaon which is on Salagar-Mangalweda road, at that time one car bearing registration No.MH-09/DA-2236 came from the opposite direction, driven by its driver in a very Smt.Sushma And Ors vs Shyamrao And Anr on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144967505/
2 high speed and negligent manner and lost control over it and dashed to the said motorcycle and caused the accident.

entities.text: Smt.Sushma And Ors vs Shyamrao And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to the accident, both of them sustained grievous injuries all over the body and the Kisan succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.

It is further contended that,
prior to the accident deceased NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB was hale and healthy, aged 45 years,
doing grocery business and was having an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In view of the sudden and untimely death of deceased, the claimants have lost their beloved family member and his earnings.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear, hence he was placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim petition and sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

7. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.8,46,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
8. We have heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the tribunal has failed to add future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contends that the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads are on the lower side.
Hence, the learned counsel seeks indulgence of this Court to allow the appeal and consequently enhance the compensation.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
He further submits that the compensation awarded by the tribunal is NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB just and proper and does not call for any interference.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.
11. It is not in dispute with regard to accident and also death of Kisan in the road traffic accident.

In order to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the car, the petitioners have produced copy of the charge sheet, marked at Ex.P5, which discloses that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
12. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged 45 years as on the date of the accident.
It is contended that he was doing grocery business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In support of the contention, the petitioners have not tendered any evidence.

sentences.text: In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income of the deceased can be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2015, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m. as per chart.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 25% has to be added towards future prospects as the deceased was aged about 45 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.10,000/.

Out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards personal expenses and therefore, the monthly income comes to Rs.7,500/-
(10,000-2500).

14. As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 45 years, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier applied to the age group of the petitioner is 14 which is rightly taken by the tribunal.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.12,60,000/-(7,500/- x 12 x 14) on account of loss of dependency as against Rs.7,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
15. In addition, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.16,500/- on account of 'loss of estate' and Rs.16,500/- towards 'funeral expenses and transportation of dead body'.
16. The petitioners are the wife, two children and mother of the deceased.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, each of the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of 'loss of consortium', which comes to Rs.1,76,000/.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7330-DB 17.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus the petitioners are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.14,69,000/- as against Rs.8,46,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,23,000/-.

18. Accordingly, we proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.

(b) The petitioners are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.14,69,000/- as against Rs.8,46,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.
(c) The petitioners are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.6,23,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount.
